name: showreel-42-snapback
style: Dark look, whole frame, calm (rule 17), cobalt colour world. ESCALATE answer 20 Nov: a new topic type (an animation that ends wrong), one bug told as a story (design/improvements.md web item 7)

voice.text: Why does your menu snap back? You tap, and it slides in. Then it jumps right back out. The fix: add forwards to the animation. The menu keeps its last frame. Look closer. Same tap, but this one stays open. Now your menus stay put.

caption:
Why does your menu snap back? 📱 You tap, the menu slides in, and at the very end of the animation it jumps right back out.

By default a CSS animation only styles the element while it runs. When it finishes, the element returns to its own style, so a menu that starts off-screen goes straight back off-screen. Add one word, forwards, and it keeps its last frame: animation: slide-in .5s forwards. Watch the reel: the top menu snaps back, the bottom one stays.

animation-fill-mode works in Chrome 43, Edge 12, Firefox 16 and Safari 9 and up, so it is safe everywhere.

Send this to whoever built your site's menu, or save it for your next slide-in panel.

sources.note: MDN animation-fill-mode (read 20 Nov 2026): sets how a CSS animation applies styles to its target before and after its execution; forwards keeps the computed values of the last keyframe; the default is none
BCD 8.1.10 (read 20 Nov 2026), css.properties.animation-fill-mode: Chrome 43, Edge 12, Firefox 16, Safari 9, iOS Safari 9

CSS Animations Level 1: with none the animation has no effect on the element before it starts and after it ends. Checked in Chrome 157 (headless, 20 Nov 2026): a translateX(-100%) element animated to 0 over .5 s sits at x -100 px after the animation with animation: slide-in .5s and at 0 px with animation: slide-in .5s forwards

tip.title: Why does your menu snap back after it slides in?
tip.why: By default (animation-fill-mode: none) a CSS animation only styles the element while it runs. When the animation ends the element goes back to its own style, so a drawer that starts off-screen jumps back off-screen the moment its slide-in finishes. animation-fill-mode: forwards keeps the computed values of the last keyframe, so the drawer stays where it landed. Supported since Chrome 43, Edge 12, Firefox 16 and Safari 9 (MDN, BCD).
tip.code:
.menu { animation: slide-in .5s; }            /* snaps back at the end */
.menu { animation: slide-in .5s forwards; }   /* stays where it landed */
